method: Read each product's own documentation at the URL shown, require a quoted span on the page, and POST one initialize to the canonical endpoint. No ranking: no product publishes usage numbers.

states.reachable: its own docs document an external/custom MCP server and the endpoint answers initialize
states.documented-not-listed: it supports MCP servers but we are not in the list/directory it reads
states.no-mcp: it does not accept an external MCP server at all
states.unverified: no primary source was found that says either way

products.what: An agent with a persistent cloud computer — browser, filesystem and terminal — that keeps working after the laptop closes and can run routines.
products.reason: Its docs document adding an MCP server that is not in the catalog, by URL or by a command.

sources.title: Use the computer and apps — Grok Bot docs (xAI)

products.what: An always-on agent in ChatGPT with its own cloud computer, scheduled runs, memories and the apps connected through Plugins.
products.reason: Dots share ChatGPT's plugin permissions, and OpenAI documents adding a custom MCP server from the Plugins tab, subject to account and workspace policy.

sources.title: Dots privacy, security, and safety FAQs — OpenAI Help Center
Connecting custom MCP servers in ChatGPT — OpenAI Help Center

products.what: Meta's personal AI agent. Its help centre documents Connectors and custom connectors created from API information.
products.reason: Meta's own Connectors page describes custom connectors but does not mention MCP; no primary source says it accepts an external MCP server.

sources.title: How Muse works with Connectors — Meta Help Centre

products.what: Anthropic's research-preview Claude that runs on its own cloud computer and uses the memory, skills and connectors already set up in Claude.
products.reason: Duet's docs say it uses the connectors set up in Claude, and Anthropic documents custom connectors over remote MCP.

sources.title: Get started with Claude Duet — Claude Help Center
Use connectors to extend Claude's capabilities — Claude Help Center

products.what: Manus's agent and connector platform. Its docs cover a connector catalog and a custom-MCP path for services that are not in it.
products.reason: Its docs document Settings → Integrations → Custom MCP Servers, adding a server by URL or command.

products.what: An open-source bot harness: named bots on several engines, each with tools, tasks and a computer, and a Bring-your-own-MCP-servers screen.
products.reason: Its docs document adding an MCP server by URL or command and turning it on after a handshake test.

sources.title: Bring your own MCP servers — OpenMausBot docs

products.what: Two open-source agent runtimes. OpenClaw's Gateway and Hermes Agent both keep an agent running and both configure external MCP servers.
products.reason: Both sets of docs document external MCP servers: OpenClaw's registry and Hermes' mcp_servers config.

sources.title: MCP (Model Context Protocol) — Hermes Agent docs

products.what: OpenBot is a local-first desktop workspace for persistent agents; Rakazo is a self-hosted agent platform with a documented remote-MCP path.
products.reason: Rakazo's docs document adding any remote MCP server at an HTTPS address.
products.note: Rakazo documents the custom-server path. OpenBot's own docs route MCP through its Marketplace apps rather than a documented add-a-server form.
